title: Getting started
body:
# Getting started: your own home on Domosenso

Build a separate Home Assistant project from the shared component catalog.

## Start here: `/onboard-home`

Clone this repository with its tags, open it in Claude Code and type `/onboard-home` (Codex: ask for
the `onboard-home` skill). The agent asks about your Home Assistant host and how you will reach it,
reads your hardware and the integrations Home Assistant discovered on your network (`domosenso
recommend --from-ha`, `domosenso discover`), recommends components and the hardware still missing,
explains the Ramka and checks your tablet if you want one, creates your home repository in a
directory outside this one, offers to keep it in a private GitHub repository, adds `backup` with values read from your Home Assistant, and stops at
`deploy production --plan`. It reads your Home Assistant freely and writes nothing to it until you
type yes. From an empty directory instead: tell the agent to read
`<catalog>/.ai/skills/onboard-home/SKILL.md` and follow it.

The rest of this page is what the skill does, step by step, for reference.

## Release status (2026-10-23)

- The selected released components have field evidence from one personal installation. This is
  an early-stage framework, not a record of completed customer projects. Check each manifest's
  `tested.homes`; an unknown count and zero tested homes mean different things.
- The supported onboarding path is **Home Assistant Container** on a Docker host reached over
  key-based SSH. Home Assistant 2026.9.2 is the checked baseline. The existing-installation path
  has been used on a Synology NAS; other hosts need validation. HAOS is not supported.
- Ramka's published `ramka/0.2.0` release supports optional climate, air, plants and photo pages.
  Its one tested layout covers 1024–1280 × 720–800 CSS px in landscape. The manifest contains
  `media_player_contract`; the documented audio integration was tested with Hegel H400 through
  `hegel_streaming`. Other players need their own contract and behavior checks.
- The host-installation path, tablet probe and HTTP proxy tools exist and have local-container
  checks. This does not establish field validation on every host or tablet. There is no
  installable scene-simulation staging environment for a new home yet.
- `remote-access` is development work: it has **no published component tag** and its manifest
  records zero tested homes as packaged. It is not included in the released website catalog.
  Do not present it as an installable release or automatically add it during onboarding.
- The framework is licensed under [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/LICENSE), including commercial use. See the
  [license scope for historical releases](/docs/licensing/). Keep your home repository private;
  the framework license does not require you to publish its configuration.

## What you need

- A Home Assistant Container you can reach over SSH with `docker` (a Synology NAS works), a
  long-lived access token from your HA profile, saved in a file outside any repository.
- On your computer: `git`, [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), `ssh` and your coding agent.
  Docker is needed on the Home Assistant host; local Docker is needed for framework checks,
  not for the normal onboarding path.
- This repository cloned, with its tags: `git clone https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso.git`, then `uv sync`
  in it (the command reads components only from tags such as `ramka/0.2.0`). You only read from
  this clone; a change to the catalog is a pull request from your fork (CONTRIBUTING.md).

## The components

| component | needs | gives you |
|---|---|---|
| `ramka` | an Android wall tablet with the HA Companion app, presence (a radar or Bermuda) | the wall-tablet dashboard: clock, weather, climate, air, plants, photos, calendar, controls |
| `backup` | — | nightly backups with retention, backup sensors, an alert when backups stop |
| `climate-air` | temperature/humidity sensors per room, a `weather` entity | indoor averages and extremes, outside figures, most humid room, lowest battery |
| `bermuda-presence` | ESPHome BLE proxies (M5Stack Atom Lite) and the Bermuda integration | which room each phone is in |
| `plants` | Mi Flora sensors | plant entities, water reminder, silent-sensor alert |
| `awnings` | Somfy RTS awnings, an ESPSomfy-RTS node | MQTT covers, wind sensor watch, sunset retract |
| `lights` | Hue rooms | room lights that follow reachable bulbs, lights-on count, lowest Hue battery |

Each component's `component.yaml` lists its inputs (your entity ids, names, rooms) and what it
provides; its `README.md` has field notes. `calendar`, `media`, `weather` describe what the Ramka reads.

## First steps (by hand)

Which components your devices satisfy, from the catalog's newest tags. With a running Home Assistant,
let it read the hardware (read-only; the token stays in its file):

```bash
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso recommend --catalog ~/path/to/domosenso --from-ha http://homeassistant.local:8123 --token-file ~/.config/ha-token
```

What Home Assistant found on your network and has set up, and whether it has an integration you
name (read-only):

```bash
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso discover --from-ha http://homeassistant.local:8123 --token-file ~/.config/ha-token --domain workday
```

Or name the devices yourself, and add what Home Assistant does not know yet the same way:

```bash
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso recommend --catalog ~/path/to/domosenso --have tapo-t315 network-audio-player
```

Then the home repository:

```bash
mkdir ~/my-home && cd ~/my-home && git init
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso init --catalog ~/path/to/domosenso
```

`init` writes `domosenso.yaml` (targets, components, local files) and a lock file. Copy
`examples/home-template/.gitignore` from the catalog into the home: it keeps `secrets.yaml`, tokens,
`.storage/`, the database and `.domosenso/` out of git.

If you want the home on GitHub, make it **private**: it names your rooms, devices and entities. Check
that `git ls-files` lists none of the ignored files above and nothing with `token` in its name. If
one is tracked, untrack it (`git rm --cached <path>`) and commit before you push. Then:

```bash
gh repo create <you>/<home name> --private --source . --remote origin --push
```

Done when `git remote -v` shows `origin`. From then on, every change goes on a branch with a pull
request.

Then, for each component you want:

```bash
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso add backup@0.1.0
# fill domosenso/backup.inputs.yaml with your values
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso render
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso status
```

Describe your Home Assistant as the `production` target in `domosenso.yaml` (SSH host, container,
config path, URL, token file). Rendered packages load only through
`homeassistant: packages: !include_dir_named packages`: copy your `configuration.yaml` from Home
Assistant into `home-assistant/configuration.yaml`, add that line if it is missing, and the deploy
carries it from then on (`secrets.yaml` and `.storage/` stay where they are). Then:

```bash
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso snapshot production --out before.json   # read-only
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso deploy production --plan                 # read-only
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso deploy production --apply --confirm <hash>
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso verify production --baseline before.json
uv run --project ~/path/to/domosenso domosenso rollback production                      # if needed
```

`deploy --plan` lists what would change, and files on your HA that the home repository does not know
about ("orphans"); decide each before `--apply`. The deploy backs up what it replaces and restores it
by itself if `check_config` fails.

Start small: `backup` first (no hardware), then one component whose hardware you have.

## With a coding agent, after onboarding

`/onboard-home` copies `examples/home-template/AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` into your home repository
and fills in the placeholders (host, container, paths). From then on open the agent in your home
repository for everyday work; it may read your Home Assistant freely and asks before any write to it.

## Giving back

A component you change or add goes back as a pull request to this repository: spec first for a new
component (`.ai/specs/`, skill `write-component-spec`), `tools/check-all.sh` green, nothing from your
household in the catalog (inputs carry it). A verified test in another home can support updating that component’s recorded field evidence.
It does not change the counts for unrelated components.

title: Compatibility and ownership
body:
# Compatibility: the contract surface of Domosenso

What a home, another component or a tool outside this repository relies on, and how much each may
change. Modelled on Open Mercato's `BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md`
([research](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/research/2026-10-20-domosenso-architecture.md) §1). A change to anything listed here
needs a spec in `.ai/specs/` first (AGENTS.md, spec-first).

## Levels

| level | what may change |
|---|---|
| **FROZEN** | nothing, short of a new major version with a migration every home runs |
| **STABLE** | nothing that breaks a home without the deprecation protocol below; additions are free |
| **ADDITIVE-ONLY** | new values, keys or fields may be added; none is removed, renamed or given a new meaning |

Versions are per component (`version:` in `component.yaml`, semantic versioning). While a
component is `0.x`, a minor version counts as the "next version" of the protocol.

## Surfaces

### Distribution

| surface | level |
|---|---|
| Tag scheme `<component>/<version>`, e.g. `bermuda-presence/0.1.0` | FROZEN |
| Remote package URL `github://zerostorypoints/domosenso/components/<id>/<path>@<component>/<version>` (ESPHome device files, `dashboard_import`; at most 255 characters) | FROZEN |
| Component ids (the directory name, `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`) | FROZEN |
| Device ids (`devices/<id>.yaml`) | STABLE |
| ESPHome `project:` name `domosenso.<component>` | STABLE |
| Card install path `www/domosenso/<id>/<version>/`, served as `/local/domosenso/<id>/<version>/` | FROZEN |

### Manifest (`component.yaml`, `schemas/component.schema.json`)

| surface | level |
|---|---|
| Required fields and their meaning: `id`, `version`, `summary`, `description_key`, `devices`, `host`, `integrations`, `artifacts`, `tested` | STABLE |
| Optional fields (`inputs`, `provides`, `consumes`, `features`, `local_only`, `photo`, artifact kinds) | ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `inputs`: each input's name, type and default | STABLE; new optional inputs are free, a new required input is a breaking change |
| `media_player_contract` of the Ramka: `required` / `optional` | STABLE; moving a feature from optional to required is a breaking change |
| Scene files (`schemas/scene.schema.json`, `scenes/README.md`) and device files; the device fields `tested` (`homes`, `note`) and `tablet` (`css`, `dpr`, `orientation`, `charge_limit`, `companion_app_tested`, `webview_tested`; only on a device of `ramka`) ([SPEC-011](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-011-2026-10-22-onboard-home-v2.md)) | ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| Match rules (`match:` in device files, `kinds/<kind>.yaml`, the `rule` of `schemas/device.schema.json` and `kind.schema.json`): field names and meaning ([SPEC-010](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-010-2026-10-22-recommend-from-ha.md)); the rules themselves are data and change freely | ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `templates/instance/**.j2`: rendered once by `domosenso add` into `config_dir/<path>` with the home's inputs, never overwritten, recorded in the lock as layer `instance`, not stamped | ADDITIVE-ONLY |

### Entities a component provides

Each entry in a manifest's `provides.entities` carries its own `stability:` (`frozen`, `stable` or
`additive-only`); the manifest is the source, this page states the rules.

- The **entity id or pattern** (`sensor.presence_<area slug>`, `input_select.<prefix>_mode`) is the
  contract, placeholders included. The slug rule is Home Assistant's: it transliterates
  (`Küche` → `kuche`).
- **Option values of a select or a state set** are part of the entity: `input_select.<prefix>_mode`
  (`off, ambient, controls, calendar`) and `input_select.<prefix>_ambient`
  (`climate, air, plants, photos, status`, in rotation order) are FROZEN.
- **Attributes** a component sets as a marker (`component:`, `area:` on the presence sensors) are
  STABLE.
- **Events** (`esphome.atom_button` with `room`, `click`) carry their own level in the manifest.
- Entity ids Home Assistant builds from a device's area and names
  (`light.<area>_ble_proxy_<room>_led`) are declared, not promised: a Home Assistant release can
  change the rule. Entities under `upstream:` belong to another integration and are not ours to
  freeze.
- An `additive-only` sensor may gain state values (`sensor.<player>_audio_quality`); consumers must
  treat an unknown value as "other".

### Cards (Lovelace resources)

| surface | level |
|---|---|
| Element names `custom:<name>-card` (agenda, air, clock-weather, corner-taps, line-style, mains, now-playing, photo-frame, plants, rooms, status, tap-button) | STABLE |
| Config keys a card's `setConfig` reads, and their meaning | STABLE; new optional keys are free |
| Resource type `module`, ES modules without a build step, JSON imported `with { type: "json" }` | STABLE |

### Translations

| surface | level |
|---|---|
| Layout `translations/<lang>.json`, `en` as source and fallback, languages `en`, `de`, `pl` | FROZEN |
| Namespaces `meta.*` (catalog text), `ui.*` (rendered dashboards), `card.*` (card runtime) | FROZEN |
| Keys a card or template uses | STABLE (renaming one breaks a home's override); new keys ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| The English wording | free; it is text, not a contract |

### Tools

| surface | level |
|---|---|
| Renderer delimiters `[[ ]]`, `[% %]`, `[# #]`; Home Assistant's own `{{ }}` / `{% %}` passed through byte-identical | FROZEN |
| Renderer inputs: globals `t(key)`, `inputs`, `lang`, `fail(message)` (ends the render with that message; SPEC-011); filter `yaml`; `*.lang.yaml.j2` → `<name>.<lang>.yaml`; an input set to `null` counts as absent | STABLE |
| First line of a rendered file: `# Rendered by Domosenso from <component>/<version> (<commit>) — do not edit` (`<commit>-dirty` when the catalog had uncommitted changes), written by `domosenso render`; the old form `# Rendered by Domosenso from <component>@<commit> — do not edit` (`domosenso_render.py --stamp`) is read as well, until the next minor version | STABLE |
| Command lines of `domosenso_render.py`, `domosenso_install.py`, `catalog_check.py`, `ha-check.sh` (and its `INPUTS=<file>` override), `esphome-check.sh`, `check-all.sh`, `agents_check.py`, `install_skills.py` | STABLE |
| Output lines agents parse: `fresh: N errors`, `config ok` / `config FAIL`, `ok` / `FAIL <step>`, `all checks passed`, `ERROR` / `WARNING` prefixes | STABLE |
| Steps of `check-all.sh` | ADDITIVE-ONLY |

### The `domosenso` command and a home repository

`uv run --project <catalog checkout> domosenso <command>`, run from the home repository's root
(`--home <dir>` otherwise). Every command prints one line per action, then `ok` or `FAIL <reason>`
(exit 0 or 1); `--json` prints the same as one document (`lines`, `data`, `result`, `reason`).
Specified in [SPEC-002](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-002-2026-10-21-whole-home-on-domosenso.md).

| surface | level |
|---|---|
| Command lines: `init --catalog`, `add <id>@<version> [--catalog-dev]`, `adopt <id>@<version>`, `render [<id>...] [--force] [--catalog-dev]`, `update <id> [--to <version>] [--force]`, `status`, `deploy <target> (--plan \| --apply) [--remove-orphans <path>...] [--prune-resources] [--confirm <hash>]`, `rollback <target> [<deploy id>]`, `snapshot <target> [--out <file>]`, `compare <a> <b> [--explain <file>]`, `verify <target> --baseline <snapshot> [--day-after]`, `recommend [--catalog <path or URL>] [--from-ha <target or URL> [--token-file <file>]] [--have <device id or kind>...]`, `discover --from-ha <target or URL> [--token-file <file>] [--domain <domain>...] [--catalog <path or URL>]`, `probe <target or URL> [--token-file <file>] (--install | --read [--wait <seconds>] | --remove)`, `http <target or URL> [--token-file <file>] (--plan | --apply --confirm <hash> | --promote) [--trusted-proxy <cidr>...]`, and `--json` on each | STABLE |
| Last line of every command: `ok` or `FAIL <reason>`; exit code 0 or 1 | STABLE |
| `FAIL` reasons agents act on: `hand-edited: <path>`, `not managed, differs: <path>`, `owned by <id>: <path>`, `tag <tag> moved: locked <sha>, now <sha>`, `<n> unclassified`, `check_config: <n> errors`, `orphan <paths>`, `not an orphan: <paths>`, `dev render: <paths>: …`, `not confirmed`, `the plan changed: its hash is now <hash>, not <given>`, `not equivalent: <n> unexplained`, `not verified: <n> failed` (the wording after the colon is free text) | STABLE |
| Lines of `render`, `add`, `update`: `write`, `same`, `dev`, `keep`, `instance`, `instance-kept`, `remove`, `stale`, `current <id> <version>`, `note <text>` (an `UPGRADE.md` line), `adopt <path>` | STABLE |
| Lines of `status`: `managed`, `managed-modified`, `instance`, `unmanaged`, `unclassified` (each `<path>`; `local` files are not listed), `component <id> <locked> newest <newest>`, `integration <name> <version> (manual)`, `missing-dashboard-entry <path>`, `unchecked <reason>` | STABLE |
| Plan lines of `deploy --plan` / `--apply`: `add`, `change`, `remove`, `orphan`, `keep` (each `<path>`), `dev-render <path>`, `resource create\|update\|unwanted\|delete <url>` (`update` adds `from <old url>`), `restart: yes\|no`, `hash <plan hash>` | STABLE |
| Apply lines: `backup <deploy id>`, `copied <n> removed <m>`, `check_config 0 errors`, `error ...` / `warning ...` (from `check_config`), `restart <target>`, `deployed <deploy id>` or `nothing to deploy`; `rollback`: `restored <n> removed <m>`, `restart <target>`, `rolled-back <deploy id>` | STABLE |
| `snapshot`: `read <part> <n>` per part, `wrote <file>` | STABLE |
| `recommend` ([SPEC-009](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-009-2026-10-22-onboard-home.md)): `fits <id>@<version> tested-homes <n\|unknown>`, `missing <id>@<version> tested-homes <n\|unknown> needs <k>`, `needs <id>@<version> <kind> [<device id>,...]`, `optional <id>@<version> <feature\|-> <kind> have\|lacks [<device id>,...]`, `describes <id>@<version>`, `unknown <token> [did-you-mean <id>,...]` (the suggestion added 2026-10-22, additive); `--json` `data`: one object per component (`id`, `version`, `fits`, `describes`, `tested_homes`, `needs`, `optional`); each `needs` and `optional` item has `recommend` and `tested_homes` (`{device id: n or null}` from the device files at the catalog's HEAD, SPEC-011) | STABLE |
| `recommend --from-ha` ([SPEC-010](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-010-2026-10-22-recommend-from-ha.md)), before the lines above: `rules <commit> devices <n> kinds <m>`, `scan devices <n> integrations <m>`, `found <device id or kind> <n> via <domain>,...`, `maybe <device id or kind> <n> via <domain>,...`, `unmatched <domain> <n>`; `found` counts as `--have`; a `maybe` also given with `--have` prints no `maybe` line; `--json` top-level `scan`: `rules_commit`, `found` and `maybe` (`{token: {count, via, devices}}`), `unmatched` (`{domain: [device index]}`), `devices` (`name`, `name_by_user`, `manufacturer`, `model`, `model_id`, `sw_version` (SPEC-011), `integrations`, `matches`) | STABLE |
| `discover` ([SPEC-011](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-011-2026-10-22-onboard-home-v2.md) §4): `discovered <domain> <n> via <source>,...`, `ignored <domain> <n>`, `configured <domain> <n>`, `failing <domain> <n> <state>`, `catalog <domain> <component>,...`, `integration <domain> <iot_class or -> <integration_type> config-flow yes\|no`, `absent <domain>`; `--json` `data`: `flows` (`handler`, `source`, `step_id`, `title_placeholders`), `entries` (`domain`, `source`, `state`, `disabled_by`, `title`), `manifests` (`{domain: {name, integration_type, iot_class, config_flow, documentation} or null}`) | STABLE; new line kinds ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `probe` (SPEC-011 §7.3): `copied <n>`, `resource create\|update <url>` (`update` adds `from <old url>`), `dashboard create\|delete domosenso-probe`, `open /domosenso-probe/0`, `removed <n>`, `warning <text>`, and from `--read` `probe viewport <w>x<h> dpr <r> screen <W>x<H> orientation <o> webview\|chromium <major or -> json-modules yes\|no dvh yes\|no user admin\|non-admin`; `FAIL no report within <s> s`; `--json` `data`: the card's report (`viewport`, `dpr`, `screen`, `orientation`, `chromium`, `webview`, `dvh`, `json_modules`, `admin`). The probe's files under `www/domosenso/_probe/`, its resource and its dashboard are not a contract | STABLE |
| `http` ([SPEC-012](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs/SPEC-012-2026-10-22-remote-access.md) §3): `http <key> <old json> -> <new json>`, `restart: yes`, `hash <hash>`, `nothing to change`, `pending waiting revert-at <time>`, `configured restart: yes\|no`, `active <slot>`, `revert-at <time\|->`, `stable`, `nothing to promote`; `FAIL` reasons `the plan changed: its hash is now <hash>, not <given>`, `the pending config failed its trial: <message>` | STABLE |
| `compare` and `verify`: per part `ok <part> (<n>)` or `FAIL <part>: <n> differences` followed by `<kind> <part> <id> [detail]` for each difference; `explanations <file> (<n>)`; `warning stale explanation <part> <id>`; the last line before `ok` is `equivalent` (`compare`) or `verified` (`verify`). Kinds: `only-in-a`, `only-in-b`, `unique-id-differs`, `not-loaded`, `config-differs`, `options-differ`, `state-changed`, `newly-unavailable`, `log-error`, `resource-missing`, `resource-duplicate`, `profile-language`, `silent-failed` | STABLE; new kinds and parts ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `deploy production --apply` asks for the word `production`; a non-interactive run needs `--confirm <plan hash>` | STABLE |
| `domosenso.yaml` (`schemas/home.schema.json`): `catalog`, `config_dir`, `esphome_dir`, `targets` (`kind` `local-docker` / `ssh-docker`), `components`, `local`, `resources`, `unmanaged_on_target`, `kiosk_users`, `custom_integrations` | STABLE; new optional keys ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `domosenso.lock` (`schemas/lock.schema.json`): per component `version`, `tag`, `commit`, `files` (`sha256`, `from`, `layer`), `resources` | STABLE; new optional keys ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `domosenso/equivalence.yaml` (`schemas/equivalence.schema.json`): explained differences between two snapshots, `after_restart: unknown` | STABLE; new optional keys ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| `domosenso/silent.yaml` (`schemas/silent.schema.json`): entry kinds `loaded_on`, `triggered_within`, `entity_fresh` | STABLE; new entry kinds ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| Snapshot file (`schemas/snapshot.schema.json`), default `.domosenso/snap/<target>.json`: `entities`, `automations`, `scripts`, `helpers`, `dashboards`, `resources`, `config_entries`, `errors`, `profiles` | STABLE; new parts ADDITIVE-ONLY |
| Home repository layout: `domosenso.yaml`, `domosenso.lock`, `domosenso/<id>.inputs.yaml`, `domosenso/equivalence.yaml`, `domosenso/silent.yaml`; `.domosenso/` is not committed | STABLE |
| Per-target deploy record `<config>/.domosenso/deployed.json` and backups `.domosenso/predeploy-<timestamp>/` | not a contract: read through `rollback`, never by hand |
| Home repository template `examples/home-template/AGENTS.md` | free: text a home copies once and then owns |

## Deprecation protocol

For a breaking change to a STABLE surface:

1. **Spec first**, saying what breaks, who is affected and the bridge.
2. **A bridge for one version.** The old name keeps working next to the new one for the next
   minor version:
   - a renamed entity → a template alias entity under the old id that mirrors the new one;
   - a renamed option value → automations and cards accept both, the helper offers the new one;
   - a renamed card config key or input → the old key is read as the new one and a warning is
     logged;
   - a renamed translation key → both keys, the old one marked deprecated.
3. **Notes.** An entry in the component's `UPGRADE.md` (what changed, what a home must do, in
   order) and a line in [UPGRADE_NOTES.md](/docs/upgrades/).
4. **Removal** of the bridge in the version after, with its own note.

A FROZEN surface does not change inside a major version. Until a component's first release to a
home other than its author's, a breaking change may skip the bridge if the upgrade note says so;
the stage 1 renames were made this way.

title: Upgrade notes
body:
# Upgrade notes

Newest first. One entry per change to a surface in [COMPATIBILITY.md](/docs/compatibility/) that a home
has to act on; the steps are in the component's own `UPGRADE.md`.

## 2026-10-22: ramka 0.2.0, optional pages and a screen size

`climate`, `air`, `plants` and `photo_dir` become optional inputs, and a new optional input `screen` names the
tablet's CSS viewport; the renderer gains the global `fail(message)`. Additive: a home needs no
action ([components/ramka/UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/UPGRADE.md)).

## 2026-10-21: the `domosenso` command and the home formats

New STABLE surfaces, no change to an existing one: the `domosenso` command lines and the output
lines agents parse, and the formats `domosenso.yaml`, `domosenso.lock`, `domosenso/equivalence.yaml`,
`domosenso/silent.yaml` and the snapshot file, each with a schema in `schemas/`
([COMPATIBILITY.md](/docs/compatibility/), "The `domosenso` command and a home repository").
`examples/home-template/AGENTS.md` is the `AGENTS.md` a home repository starts from. Homes need no
action; a home that renders by hand adopts the command with `domosenso adopt <id>@<version>`.

## 2026-10-21: stamp line names the tag

The first line of a rendered file changes from `# Rendered by Domosenso from <id>@<commit> — do not
edit` to `# Rendered by Domosenso from <id>/<version> (<commit>) — do not edit`, so it names the
tag the file was rendered from (`<commit>-dirty` inside the parentheses when the catalog had
uncommitted changes). The `domosenso` command reads both forms and writes the new one; the old tool
`tools/domosenso_render.py --stamp` still writes the old form. Homes need no action: the next
`domosenso render` rewrites the first line. The old form is read until the next minor version.

## 2026-10-21: remote package URL

The account in the remote package URL changes from `domosenso` to `zerostorypoints`, the account the
repository lives under: `github://domosenso/domosenso/components/<id>/<path>@<component>/<version>`
becomes `github://zerostorypoints/domosenso/components/<id>/<path>@<component>/<version>`, in device
files, `package_import_url` and blueprint `source_url`. The change comes before any home used the
URL, so no bridge is kept (the rule for components not yet used by another home, in
[COMPATIBILITY.md](/docs/compatibility/)). A device file that still uses the old form must be changed
to the new one.

## 2026-10-22: ramka 0.1.2

- **ramka 0.1.2** ([components/ramka/UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/UPGRADE.md)): metadata only
  (`tested.homes`); nothing to do, a home may stay on 0.1.1.

## 2026-10-21: ramka 0.1.1

- **ramka 0.1.1** ([components/ramka/UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/UPGRADE.md)): "Tomorrow" capitalised
  in en and de; the cards move to `www/domosenso/ramka/0.1.1/` and the twelve resource URLs change in
  place to `/local/domosenso/ramka/0.1.1/cards/<name>.js`.

## 2026-10-20: stage 1, the catalog

The first versions of the components, moved out of one home's configuration. No home ran a released
version before, so no bridge was kept: each rename below breaks a home that used the old name until
it follows the steps.

- **ramka 0.1.0** ([components/ramka/UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/UPGRADE.md)):
  - helper option values are English: `input_select.<prefix>_mode` `kalendarz → calendar`;
    `input_select.<prefix>_ambient` `temperatury → climate`, `powietrze → air`, `rosliny → plants`,
    `zdjecia → photos` (`off`, `ambient`, `controls`, `status` unchanged);
  - the entity prefix is an input; entities renamed so that none names a player or a language
    (`binary_sensor.<prefix>_hegel_playing → binary_sensor.<prefix>_media_playing`,
    `input_text.ramka_zdjecie → input_text.<prefix>_photo`, `image.ramka → image.<prefix>_photo`,
    the shell commands `<prefix>_index` / `<prefix>_pick`);
  - package and dashboard are rendered from templates, one dashboard per language;
  - the cards install under `www/domosenso/ramka/0.1.0/` and each Lovelace resource's URL changes in
    place to `/local/domosenso/ramka/0.1.0/cards/<name>.js`;
  - restart Home Assistant rather than reloading the input_selects (a reload keeps a state that is
    no longer an option).
- **bermuda-presence 0.1.0** ([docs/pilot-bermuda-presence.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/pilot-bermuda-presence.md)): from the
  pilot. Device files pull the packages at the tag `bermuda-presence/0.1.0`; the room sensors and the
  offline alert are blueprint instances in the home's instance layer, with the entity ids
  `sensor.presence_<area slug>` and `automation.ble_proxy_offline` a home had before.
- **Every other component 0.1.0** (awnings, calendar, climate-air, lights, media, plants, weather):
  catalog entries describing what the Ramka reads; nothing for a home to change.

title: Contributing
body:
# Contributing to Domosenso

For people and agents who change Domosenso itself: the catalog, the `domosenso` command, the skills
and the documents. If you want to run your own home on it, start with the [README](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/README.md).
Agents: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/AGENTS.md) is the full rule set; this page is the map.

## Your first contribution

The usual first one is a device the catalog does not know yet, such as a network player for the
Ramka: [docs/integrate-a-device.md](/docs/integrate-a-device/) walks through it, with the Hegel
integration as the worked example (skill `new-integration`).

## How changes land

- **A pull request from your fork.** Fork the repository (`gh repo fork zerostorypoints/domosenso
  --clone` also sets the `upstream` remote), make one branch per change
  (`feat/…`, `fix/…`, `docs/…`), keep it current with `git pull --rebase upstream main`, and open a
  pull request into `main`. Maintainers review and merge; nothing reaches `main` any other way, and
  published tags never move.
- **Spec first** for a new component, a new capability of the command, a schema change or anything in
  [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](/docs/compatibility/): a spec in `.ai/specs/` (skill `write-component-spec`),
  approved, then built. A fix that keeps the contract goes straight to a pull request with a test.
- **A plan with several pull requests** has a coordinator session and a feature branch (AGENTS.md,
  "Plans that span several pull requests").
- **Privacy.** Nothing from a real home: no real names, rooms, entity ids, addresses, photos or floor
  plans; examples use the demo home (Alex and Sam). `tests/test_catalog_content.py::test_privacy`
  checks it. The one exception is the maintainer's own Ramka photos in `.github/readme/`.
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green before a pull request.

## Layout

```
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md    instructions for coding agents (CLAUDE.md only imports AGENTS.md)
.ai/skills/, .ai/specs/ agent skills (linked into .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/) and specs
components/<id>/        the catalog: manifest (component.yaml), esphome/, ha/, cards/, translations/,
                        README.md (field notes)
devices/<id>.yaml       the hardware the components name: names, description and what it does (en, de, pl),
                        and how Home Assistant shows it (match rules)
kinds/<kind>.yaml       how Home Assistant shows a kind of hardware (match rules for `recommend --from-ha`)
scenes/<id>.yaml        the demo's eight scenes: time, entity states and attributes, what the tablet shows,
                        who takes part (format and rules: scenes/README.md)
examples/demo-home/     a fictional home (Alex and Sam) as an instance of the catalog: inputs, states, generated media
tools/                  checks that run a component against ESPHome and Home Assistant
docs/                   framework design: research, the pilot write-up, specs and plans
```

Nothing from a real household belongs here: no real names, rooms, entity ids, addresses, photos,
calendars or floor plans. A real home lives in its own repository.

## Components

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| [awnings](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/awnings/component.yaml) | Somfy RTS awnings through an ESPSomfy-RTS radio node, with the awnings' wind sensor |
| [backup](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/backup/component.yaml) | Nightly backups with rolling retention, backup sensors and a stale alert |
| [remote-access](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/remote-access/component.yaml) | Home Assistant from anywhere through a Cloudflare Tunnel: no open port, a country allow-list |
| [bermuda-presence](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/bermuda-presence/component.yaml) | Room-level presence of phones and tablets from BLE proxies and Bermuda |
| [calendar](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/calendar/component.yaml) | Calendar events from a CalDAV server |
| [climate-air](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/climate-air/component.yaml) | Room temperature and humidity (Tapo), air quality (Ruuvi Air) |
| [lights](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/lights/component.yaml) | Philips Hue lights per room |
| [media](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/media/component.yaml) | A network audio player as a media player (tested: Hegel H400) |
| [plants](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/plants/component.yaml) | Houseplant sensors (Xiaomi Mi Flora) |
| [ramka](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/component.yaml) | Wall tablet: radar wake-up, ambient pages, music, awnings, lights, calendar ([upgrade notes](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/UPGRADE.md)) |
| [weather](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/weather/component.yaml) | Weather and forecast from Met.no |

## Agent skills

One source in `.ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, linked for Claude Code (`.claude/skills/`) and Codex and
Cursor (`.agents/skills/`) by `uv run tools/install_skills.py`.

| skill | use it to |
|---|---|
| [onboard-home](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/skills/onboard-home/SKILL.md) | start a new home: interview, recommend components, `domosenso init`, add `backup`, stop at `deploy production --plan` |
| [check](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/skills/check/SKILL.md) | run `tools/check-all.sh` and report pass or fail per step |
| [new-component](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/skills/new-component/SKILL.md) | scaffold `components/<id>/` and get the checker and tests passing |
| [new-integration](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/skills/new-integration/SKILL.md) | bring a device the catalog lacks: find or write its integration, add it to the catalog in a PR |
| [write-component-spec](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/skills/write-component-spec/SKILL.md) | write a spec in `.ai/specs/` and stop for approval |
| [render-and-stage](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/skills/render-and-stage/SKILL.md) | render a component into a home repository, install it, check it, try it on staging |

## Checks

They need Docker or `uv` and flash nothing. Run from the repository root.

```bash
tools/check-all.sh                           # all of the below: agents_check, pytest, npm test,
                                             # catalog_check, ha-check and esphome-check for every component
uv run tools/agents_check.py                 # AGENTS.md within 32,768 bytes, CLAUDE.md, skills and their links
uv run tools/install_skills.py               # links .ai/skills/ for claude-code, codex and cursor
tools/esphome-check.sh bermuda-presence      # config of the demo-home device files using it, and the factory image
tools/esphome-check.sh bermuda-presence compile ble-proxy-dining.yaml   # also compile
tools/ha-check.sh bermuda-presence           # check_config on a fresh home; needs docker
uv run tools/catalog_check.py --strict       # manifests, translations, devices, scenes
uv run tools/make_demo_media.py              # rewrites examples/demo-home/media/ (generated images)
tools/ha-check.sh ramka                      # renders examples/demo-home/inputs/ramka.yaml first
uv run tools/domosenso_render.py components/ramka --inputs examples/demo-home/inputs/ramka.yaml --out <dir> [--stamp]
uv run tools/domosenso_install.py components/ramka --config <config dir>   # cards, shell scripts, theme
```

`--stamp` makes the first line of every rendered file
`# Rendered by Domosenso from <component>@<commit> — do not edit`. A component's cards install
under `www/domosenso/<id>/<version>/` (`artifacts.install_path`), so a new version gets new
`/local/` URLs and the browser's 31-day cache cannot mix versions.

`tools/esphome-check.sh` builds a throwaway git remote from the working tree, tagged
`<component>/<version>`, and rewrites the demo home's `github://` packages to it; `tools/ha-check.sh`
loads the component's blueprints and the demo-home instance into a minimal Home Assistant
configuration and runs `check_config` in the `homeassistant/home-assistant:2026.9.2` image.

Dependencies: `uv sync` (Python: jinja2, pyyaml and jsonschema for the tools, pytest and pillow
for development) and `npm install` (happy-dom, for `npm test`; node 22 or newer).

## Documents

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/AGENTS.md): how to work in this repository, for people and agents
- [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](/docs/compatibility/): the contract surface and the deprecation protocol;
  [docs/UPGRADE_NOTES.md](/docs/upgrades/): what changed for homes
- [docs/home-assistant-notes.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/home-assistant-notes.md), [docs/integration-notes.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/integration-notes.md): field notes
- [.ai/specs/](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/.ai/specs): specs, SPEC-NNN-<date>-<title>.md

- [docs/research/2026-10-20-domosenso-architecture.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/research/2026-10-20-domosenso-architecture.md)
- [docs/pilot-bermuda-presence.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/pilot-bermuda-presence.md): the catalog format tried on one component
- [docs/2026-10-20-domosenso-demo-staging-i18n-design.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/2026-10-20-domosenso-demo-staging-i18n-design.md): design for the demo, staging and translations
- [docs/2026-10-20-domosenso-stage1-catalog-foundation.md](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/docs/2026-10-20-domosenso-stage1-catalog-foundation.md): the stage 1 plan

## License and contributions

Original DomoSenso code and documentation are licensed under [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/LICENSE),
with copyright 2026 ZeroStoryPoints GmbH. Unless you explicitly state otherwise,
contributions intentionally submitted for inclusion are provided under the same
license, as described in section 5. Only submit material you have the right to

The code license does not grant rights to use DomoSenso or ZeroStoryPoints trade

title: Integrate a device
body:
# Integrate a device

For a device the catalog does not know yet. Four steps; most devices stop at the first or the
second. The example task throughout is a **Naim Uniti Star** streamer for the `media` component (the
Ramka's music view). Nobody has run the Naim through this guide yet: every Naim value below that
nobody has seen is marked *not tried yet*, and the first home that has one fills them in with its
pull request. The worked example for step 3 is the Hegel H400 amplifier and its integration,
[hegel-home-assistant](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant).

Domosenso never installs integrations itself. Home Assistant's own integrations come with it, and
custom ones are installed through [HACS](https://hacs.xyz); a component's manifest only names the
integration it needs.

## 1. What Home Assistant already has

Ask Home Assistant what it found on your network and what it has set up:

```bash
uv run --project <catalog> domosenso discover --catalog <catalog> --from-ha <HA URL> --token-file <token file>
uv run --project <catalog> domosenso recommend --catalog <catalog> --from-ha <HA URL> --token-file <token file>
```

`discover` lists the integrations Home Assistant discovered and has set up; `recommend` lists the
devices it matched to the catalog and the ones it could not place (`unmatched`, per integration).
The same discoveries are in Home Assistant under Settings → Devices & services → Discovered.

Look for a built-in integration first. For an audio player that means Google Cast, DLNA (`dlna_dmr`),
Spotify Connect or the maker's own integration. The `media` component needs a `media_player` that
meets the Ramka's contract (`media_player_contract` in [the Ramka's manifest](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/ramka/component.yaml)):

- required: `state`, `turn_on`, `turn_off`, `media_play`, `media_pause`, `volume_level`, `volume_set`;
- optional: `volume_step`, `previous_track`, `next_track`, `media_title`, `media_artist`,
  `media_album_name`, `entity_picture`, `media_position`.

Check it in Developer tools → States (the entity's `supported_features` and attributes) and by
trying each action from Developer tools → Actions, once while the player is playing and once from
standby. Turning on from standby is where generic integrations most often fall short.

*Naim, not tried yet:* the Uniti Star has Chromecast built in and plays as a UPnP renderer, so Home
Assistant may offer it through Google Cast and DLNA. Whether either turns it on from standby and sets
its volume is the first thing to find out.

**Done when:** you know which integration gives the device's `media_player` and whether it meets the
contract. If a built-in one does, skip to step 4.

## 2. HACS

Search HACS (its Integrations list) and GitHub for the device's name with "home assistant". Before
installing, read:

- the README: which models it was tried on, local or cloud, what it needs from you;
- the tests and CI: a `tests/` folder and a passing workflow;
- the last release and the open issues: a year without a release, while Home Assistant changes
  monthly, is a risk.

Install it through HACS, restart Home Assistant, add it under Settings → Devices & services, and
check it against the contract as in step 1.

*Naim, not tried yet:* the candidate is `naim_media_player` from
[jorourke/naim-atom-home-assistant](https://github.com/jorourke/naim-atom-home-assistant), a HACS
custom repository written for the Uniti Atom and not yet tried on a Uniti Star. Two others exist for
other Naim lines (`peteS-UK/naim_streamer`, `blitzkopf/naim_muso`).

**Done when:** an integration from HACS gives the device's `media_player`, you noted the version you
tested, and it meets the contract; or you found nothing that does.

## 3. Write one

Only if nothing fits. A Home Assistant integration is a Python package under
`custom_components/<domain>/`, published as its own public repository so that HACS can install it.
The Hegel integration is a small, complete example (about 1,300 lines of Python); every link below
points at its release `v0.1.7`.

| Part | In Hegel | What to take from it |
|---|---|---|
| Layout and HACS | [`hacs.json`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/hacs.json), [`custom_components/hegel_streaming/`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/tree/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming) | One integration per repository, at that path. `hacs.json` names it and the oldest Home Assistant it supports. |
| Manifest | [`manifest.json`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/manifest.json) | `domain`, `config_flow: true`, `integration_type: device`, `iot_class: local_push`, `version` (HACS requires it), and a `zeroconf` entry so Home Assistant offers the device when it appears on the network. |
| API client | [`api.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/api.py) | All network talk in one class over Home Assistant's shared `aiohttp` session, no extra requirements. Two kinds of error: the device did not answer (`HegelConnectionError`), or it answered something unexpected (`HegelError`). The module docstring records the device's API as found. |
| Config flow and discovery | [`config_flow.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/config_flow.py) | Set up by address or from zeroconf. The device's own id is the unique id, so a new IP address is followed instead of creating a second device, and a repair issue suggests reserving the address. `reconfigure` changes the address and refuses a different device. |
| Coordinator: push or poll | [`coordinator.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/coordinator.py) | The amp keeps an event queue: a background task long-polls it and applies each change at once; a full refresh every 30 s is the safety net, and an expired queue is re-created with a refresh. A device without events would poll only. |
| Entities | [`media_player.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/media_player.py), [`sensor.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/sensor.py), [`binary_sensor.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/binary_sensor.py), [`entity.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/entity.py) | The `media_player`; sensors for the stream (quality, codec, sample rate, bit depth, bitrate, streaming service); a connectivity sensor. A shared base entity holds the device info. |
| Off versus not responding | [`coordinator.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/coordinator.py), [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/__init__.py) | An amp switched off at the mains does not answer. It is reported as off, not unavailable, so dashboards and automations keep working, and the device info cached in the entry lets setup succeed while it is off. The log says once that it stopped answering and once that it is back. |
| Options | [`config_flow.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/config_flow.py) (`HegelOptionsFlow`) | A volume cap, inputs to hide, input names; the entry reloads when they change. |
| Translations | [`translations/`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/tree/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/translations) | Every string the user sees, `en.json` first. |
| Diagnostics | [`diagnostics.py`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/custom_components/hegel_streaming/diagnostics.py) | The file behind "Download diagnostics": entry, device, inputs, last state. Ask for it in bug reports. |
| Tests with a fake device | [`tests/`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/tree/v0.1.7/tests) | `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component`; `conftest.py` holds answers trimmed from a real H400, so the tests run without the amp. |
| CI | [`validate.yml`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/.github/workflows/validate.yml), [`tests.yml`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/blob/v0.1.7/.github/workflows/tests.yml) | `hassfest` and the HACS action on every push and weekly; ruff and pytest on every push. |
| Releases | [releases](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/hegel-home-assistant/releases) | A tag `vX.Y.Z` matching `manifest.json`'s `version`, with a GitHub release; HACS offers releases as updates. |

**Done when:** the repository is public, its CI is green, a tagged release exists, and HACS installs it
as a custom repository on your own Home Assistant, where the player meets the contract.

## 4. Bring the device into the catalog

Now the catalog learns the device, so `recommend --from-ha` finds it in the next home. This is a pull
request from your fork into this repository (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](/docs/contributing/)).

**A device file**, `devices/<id>.yaml`, like [`devices/hegel-h400.yaml`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/devices/hegel-h400.yaml):

```yaml
id: hegel-h400
names: {en: Hegel H400, de: Hegel H400, pl: Hegel H400}
description_key: meta.devices.hegel-h400.description
does_key: meta.devices.hegel-h400.does
photo: null
component: media
tested: {homes: 1}
# Seen on HA 2026.9.2: manufacturer Hegel, model H400, through hegel_streaming.
match:
  - integration: hegel_streaming
    model: "*H400*"
```

`match` rules compare the integration domain, `manufacturer`, `model` and `model_id` that Home
Assistant reports for the device (glob patterns, case-insensitive). Take them from `recommend
--from-ha --json`, where the device shows up under `unmatched`, and write down the Home Assistant
version you saw them on. The description and "does" texts go into the component's
`translations/en.json`, `de.json` and `pl.json`.

*Naim, not tried yet:* the integration domain, manufacturer and model strings Home Assistant reports
for a Uniti Star are unknown until someone runs `recommend --from-ha` with one.

**The component** that uses the device, here [`components/media/component.yaml`](https://github.com/zerostorypoints/domosenso/blob/817f8de4eebce9563b385294376e6b751c01ef9f/components/media/component.yaml),
gets the device id under `devices.requires[].recommend`. If the device needs an integration from
HACS, the manifest lists it under `integrations` with `source: hacs`, `repo` and the `tested` version.

**A second integration is a contract change.** `integrations` is a flat list that means "all of
these": adding `naim_media_player` next to `hegel_streaming` would read as a home needing both. An
alternative integration for an existing component needs a new way to say it in the manifest (for
example integrations tied to a device, or a "one of" group). That is spec first: write it with the
`write-component-spec` skill, in your own pull request, before the manifest changes.

What the Ramka shows for a player without Hegel's extra sensors: the quality, source and details
fields stay empty, and previous/next are always shown (the Ramka hides them only while
`media_service_sensor` reads a service that cannot skip). All of these inputs are optional.

Then `tools/check-all.sh` green and a pull request into `main`. The device is tested in one home:
yours.

**Done when:** the pull request is merged and `recommend --from-ha` on your Home Assistant lists the
device under the component instead of under `unmatched`.
